entities.summary: Sextus Pompeius Magnus Pius, known in English as Sextus Pompey, was a Roman military leader who upheld the cause of his father, Pompey the Great, against Julius Caesar and his supporters during the last civil wars of the Roman Republic. Born into a prominent family, Pompey was destined for greatness, and his early life was marked by his involvement in the Roman naval war against Mithridates VI of Pontus. As a key figure in the Second Triumvirate, Pompey played a crucial role in the defeat of Brutus and Cassius, two of Caesar's assassins. His legacy, however, was short-lived, as he was executed by Octavian's soldiers in 34 BCE. Despite his tragic end, Pompey's impact on Roman history cannot be overstated, as he paved the way for the rise of the Roman Empire and shaped the course of the Roman Republic's decline. The year 34 BCE marked the end of an era, as the Roman Republic succumbed to the increasing power of the Roman Empire, and Pompey's fate served as a warning to future generations of the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of loyalty to the state.
